description: An alias after AS takes a wider vocabulary than a column reference: case, cast, constraint, cross, default, inner, join and when are legal as select-item and table aliases (and a table alias qualifies columns) though illegal as column references, while truly reserved words (select, from, where, order) stay refused. Converted 1:1 from ddl/AliasKeywordTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE ak (x NUMBER)
INSERT INTO ak VALUES (7)
SELECT x AS case FROM ak
SELECT x AS cast FROM ak
SELECT x AS constraint FROM ak
SELECT x AS cross FROM ak
SELECT x AS default FROM ak
SELECT x AS inner FROM ak
SELECT x AS join FROM ak
SELECT x AS when FROM ak
CREATE TABLE ak (x NUMBER)
INSERT INTO ak VALUES (7)
SELECT x FROM ak AS case
SELECT x FROM ak AS cast
SELECT x FROM ak AS constraint
SELECT x FROM ak AS cross
SELECT x FROM ak AS default
SELECT x FROM ak AS inner
SELECT x FROM ak AS join
SELECT x FROM ak AS when
CREATE TABLE ak (x NUMBER)
INSERT INTO ak VALUES (7)
SELECT inner.x FROM ak AS inner
CREATE TABLE ak (x NUMBER)
INSERT INTO ak VALUES (7)
SELECT x AS c FROM ak AS t
SELECT x AS auto FROM ak AS limit
CREATE TABLE ak (x NUMBER)
INSERT INTO ak VALUES (7)
SELECT x AS select FROM ak
SELECT x AS from FROM ak
SELECT x AS where FROM ak
SELECT x AS order FROM ak
